title: Neuraxial Anesthesia — Spinal & Epidural
sources: Critical Vector — Anesthesia Reference: Neuraxial CI / Spinal Agents / Spinal Hypotension / Epidural Levels / High-Total Spinal
ASRA 2022 (5th ed) + 2025 update on neuraxial procedures in the anticoagulated patient; standard obstetric-anesthesia practice

changelog.change: Initial entry — contraindications, spinal agent + adjunct doses (incl. the standard C/S mix), spinal-hypotension prevention/treatment (norepinephrine now first-line in OB), epidural levels + the urgent-C/S top-up, high/total spinal management, and PDPH.

summary: Spinal hypotension: CO-load (not pre-load) 500–1000 mL at block placement and start a prophylactic vasopressor infusion — norepinephrine 0.05–0.1 mcg/kg/min is now first-line for obstetric spinal (better HR maintenance than phenylephrine). Anticoagulant hold times before a neuraxial or deep block live in the neuraxial-anticoagulation module.

items: Absolute: patient refusal; coagulopathy (INR > 1.5, platelets < 80 ×10⁹/L per ASRA 2023) or active therapeutic anticoagulation within the ASRA hold window; infection at the puncture site; raised ICP / an intracranial mass (herniation risk); no resuscitation equipment / monitoring.

Relative: hypovolaemia (stabilise first); severe fixed-output lesions (severe AS or MS — a fall in SVR drops CO); systemic sepsis / bacteraemia (individualise); pre-existing neurological disease (document the baseline); indeterminate surgical duration.

rows: AVOID for spinal — transient neurological symptoms; use chloroprocaine instead

body.text: Intrathecal adjuncts (preservative-free): fentanyl 10–25 mcg (intra-op analgesia, reduces LA dose); morphine 50–300 mcg (post-op analgesia — DELAYED respiratory depression 6–18 h, monitor 18–24 h); hydromorphone 50–100 mcg (~12 h monitoring); epinephrine 100–200 mcg (+30–50% duration, test-dose component); clonidine 15–75 mcg or dexmedetomidine 3–10 mcg (prolong the block, cause hypotension / bradycardia / sedation). Standard C/S mix: hyperbaric bupivacaine 0.75% 10–12 mg + fentanyl PF 10–15 mcg + morphine PF 100–150 mcg ± epinephrine 100–200 mcg.

items: Prevention: CO-load 500–1000 mL crystalloid AT block placement (not before — a pre-load redistributes). Start a prophylactic phenylephrine 25–50 mcg/min or norepinephrine 0.05–0.1 mcg/kg/min infusion with the block. Ondansetron 4 mg IV blunts the vasovagal (Bezold-Jarisch) component.

Treatment: phenylephrine 50–200 mcg IV bolus → 25–100 mcg/min infusion. Norepinephrine 5–10 mcg IV bolus → 0.05–0.1 mcg/kg/min — OB-preferred (less reflex bradycardia). Ephedrine 5–10 mg IV if bradycardia coexists. Atropine 0.5 mg for isolated bradycardia — low threshold for epinephrine if it doesn't respond. Fluid bolus if hypovolaemic. Left uterine displacement in the parturient.
2024 OB update: norepinephrine is equivalent or superior to phenylephrine for obstetric spinal hypotension (better HR maintenance, similar neonatal outcomes) — consider it first-line where available.

rows: PCEA 0.0625–0.1% bupivacaine + fentanyl 2 mcg/mL; 5 mL bolus / 10 min lockout / 8 mL/hr basal
Programmed intermittent bolus 0.0625–0.1% bupivacaine 5–10 mL / 30 min, or PCEA
PCEA 0.0625% bupivacaine + fentanyl 2 mcg/mL; 5–8 mL bolus / 15 min lockout / 6–10 mL/hr basal

body.text: Urgent C/S top-up from a working labour epidural: 2% lidocaine + epinephrine 1:200,000, 15–20 mL in 5 mL increments q3–5 min; add sodium bicarbonate 1 mEq per 10 mL to speed onset (~10–15 min). Alternative: 0.5% bupivacaine 15–20 mL (slower). Always aspirate and give a test dose; watch for LAST and for a high block.

Rapid unexpected cephalad spread: upper-limb numbness / weakness → dyspnoea, dysphonia, apnoea → bradycardia + hypotension → loss of consciousness / arrest (total spinal). Call for help + the code cart, tell the surgeons. Support ventilation, intubate if apnoeic. Epinephrine 10 mcg IV boluses titrated up for bradycardia / hypotension; atropine 0.5 mg for mild bradycardia (low threshold for epinephrine); fluids wide open. Parturient: immediate LUD, alert OB, prepare for a perimortem C/S, and run the maternal-cardiac-arrest protocol if she arrests.

items: Positional (worse upright, better supine) frontal / occipital headache ± neck stiffness, photophobia, tinnitus, diplopia — onset within 5 days of a dural puncture.
Conservative for 24–48 h: bed rest as tolerated, hydration, analgesia, caffeine 300 mg PO; a bilateral sphenopalatine ganglion block is a reasonable low-risk step.
Epidural blood patch is the definitive treatment: 15–20 mL of autologous blood, then lie flat for 1–2 h. ~ 70–90% relief; repeat once if it recurs.
Always consider the sinister differential for a NEW postpartum / post-procedure headache that loses its postural character — cerebral venous sinus thrombosis, subdural haematoma, PRES, pre-eclampsia.
